description:
Without bike lane view (drawing not to scale): Plan of perpendicular on-street motorcycle stalls along a curb. The face of curb runs horizontally across the upper part of the view, and a large arrow at the lower left marks DIRECTION OF VEHICULAR TRAVEL (pointing left). At the left, red curb is shown on the curb line, with an 8' dimension from the left stall line to the next stall line, and a PARKING METER (dot) 20" from the face of curb and 3' from the first stall line. Stall lines are 4" (TYP.) white and each runs 1'-6" at the left end, with the base lines 8' (TYP) from the face of curb. A 19' dimension runs from the left stall line to the left edge of the first red curb box. The red curb box (labeled R/C, 5' wide) is filled with a 45 degree diagonal pattern with three circled K symbols and outlined by 4" white lines. To its right are three vertical 4" white stall lines, the legend MOTORCYCLE (callout 8" TALL WHITE STENCILS) with 8' (TYP) beneath it, and dashes along the base line. A second red curb box with three K symbols closes the right end (callout 4" WHITE LINES AT 45 DEGREES), with a 1'-4" dimension at its stall line. The overall dimension "A" is measured between the two boxes at the bottom. Above the curb, spacing is 5', 4'-6", 4'-6", 4'-6", 4'-6" and 2' from the left red curb box to the right end. Sign A (R/A) is posted at the left end, Sign B is posted on the post of the two parking meters (callout SIGN B ON POST PARKING METERS, meter 20" from curb), and Sign A (L/A) is posted at the right end. At the far right, the curb ends with a break symbol, a CURB RETURN, a CROSS STREET and a RED CURB callout.

With bike lane view (drawing not to scale): The same layout is repeated lower on the sheet with a bike lane added. The stall base line is one continuous 4" line (4" TYP.) 8' (TYP) from the curb face, with 1'-4" at the left end stall line and a 19' dimension. A hatched 6" W line (6" white marking) runs parallel to the curb below the stalls. In the bike lane, a left-pointing arrow and the words BIKE LANE are stenciled. A 2' dimension is shown at the right below the right red curb box. The signs and meters repeat as above, with Sign A (R/A) at the left and Sign A (printed L/R) at the right, Sign B on the meter posts, 20" meter offsets and 5', 4'-6" and 2' spacings, then the red curb, curb return and cross street.

Sign legend: Sign A (R/A right arrow and L/A left arrow) is R32F (CA), a green on white sign reading 2 HOUR PARKING 8AM-6PM with small text MOTORCYCLE PARKING ONLY and a green arrow. Sign B is a white sign with black border reading MOTORCYCLE PARKING ONLY, (6" x 8" min).

Table, MOTORCYCLE STALL LAYOUT (stalls and dimension "A"): 2 stalls: 9'. 3 stalls: 13.5'. 4 stalls: 18'. 5 stalls: 22.5'. 6 stalls: 27'.

Legend: solid black bar = red curb. Hatched bar = 6" white marking. Solid bar = 4" white marking.

description: Text sheet: This is a notes-only page with no drawing. It is divided into three headed lists. Section A, Installation Notes, has 9 numbered items. Section B, Motorcycle Parking Stalls (MPS), refers back to Note A-5 and has 8 numbered items. Section C, Miscellaneous, has 1 item. Note A-6 carries the circled K symbol used on the layout sheet. The title block reads City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, ON-STREET MOTORCYLE PARKING STALLS (as printed), Drawing No. S-404.2, sheet 3 of 3.
notes:
A. Installation notes:
1. Parking meters may be replaced with a Pay Station Kiosk, and space numbering at the curb of each stall.
2. All parking stall lines and edge lines shall be in Alkyd-based Thermoplastic in accordance with the current LADOT specifications.
3. "MOTORCYCLE" pavement messages shall be in paint in accordance with the current LADOT specifications.
4. Motorcycle stalls should be installed at the beginning and/or at the end of the block, adjacent to the required intersection red curb.
5. Motorcycle stalls shall not be considered on severe slope. Angled stalls are preferred for ease of access, unless noted otherwise per engineering recommendation. Existing road condition and other factors will determine which style (angled vs. perpendicular) stall will be installed.
6. (K) = K71 bollards or candlestick delineators (optional) may be installed at locations not affected by street cleaning operations. Space at equal distance on the center within the box from the curb to the 4" white lines.
7. There shall be at least one set of motorcycle stalls and no more than three sets connected in parallel at each installation. Each set consists of two motorcycle stalls.
8. Motorcycle stall marking may also be used in non-metered spaces. Notes #2 through #6 above apply.
9. Two meter heads shall be installed on a yoke on one single meter post for each set of metered motorcycle stalls.

B. Motorcycle parking stalls (MPS): (See Note A-5)
1. Parking meter heads, posts and signs shall be removed or adjusted as needed if MPS are installed in a parking meter zone.
2. Rubberized wheel-stops may be used in between the MPS zones and an on-street parking space to supplement bollards and/or delineators.
3. Minimum clearance from the top of a driveway to a MPS zone shall be 6'.
4. Minimum clearance from a fire hydrant to a MPS zone shall be 15'.
5. Minimum clearance from a parallel or perpendicular vehicle parking space shall be at least 5' as measured at the curb and at least 10' minimum clearance from an angle vehicle parking space.
6. MPS zones shall not be considered adjacent to any commercial loading zone or any bus zones.
7. MPS zones shall not be installed within any minimum required intersection red curb.
8. Signs similar to R32F(CA) with arrow, in the MUTCD (CA) can be installed in lieu at the beginning and at the end of the MPS zone.

C. Miscellaneous
1. All pavement markings shall be skid-resistant.

description:

Dotted yellow cat tracks, labeled 4"Y (NOTE 2), curve through the middle of the intersection joining the opposing lanes, drawn as short dashes about the intersection center.

Upper left corner: a TRAP RIGHT TURN LANE with a right-turn arrow on the vertical street approach. A callout SEE NOTE 8 points to the crosswalk edge at the curb return, and SEE NOTE 4 points to the point EC where the curb return curve ends, with a 90 degree radial line and radius R3 drawn from the curve center to EC and to the BC point at the lower end of the left curb.
Lower left: an ADDED RIGHT TURN LANE on the left street approach with a right-turn arrow, curving to the right at the curb return.
Upper right: a second TRAP RIGHT TURN LANE (right-turn arrow) on the right street approach. Curve points EC, ECR, BCR and BC are labeled at the curb return with radius R2 and 90 degree radial lines. SEE NOTE 3 is called out at the crosswalk line on the vertical street.
Lower right: curb return with ECR, ECR (as printed ECR/EC) and radius R1, a PARKED VEHICLE (car symbol) in the parking lane on the right approach, with a 90 degree radial line at the end of curve. A SEE NOTE 4 callout is at BC on the bottom street, a 15' TYP. dimension is shown along the stop line at the curb return, and a SEE NOTE 5 callout and an ADDED RIGHT TURN LANE (right-turn arrow) are shown on the bottom approach with BC and BCR points and radius R1. Left-turn arrows are shown in the left-turn lanes on the bottom leg.

Special double turn detail: A separate partial plan labeled SPECIAL DOUBLE TURN DETAIL at the bottom of the sheet. On the upper approach (vertical street) the lanes are marked with left-turn, through and right-turn arrows. A bracket labeled NO.1 LANE WIDTH shows the first lane and CURB LANE (OR NO.2 & NO.3 COMBINED) WIDTH shows the curb lane width, with a 1' dimension at the line offset and the note 20' MINIMUM WITH PARKING, 12' MINIMUM WITH NO PARKING (SEE NOTE 6). This is repeated on the left approach (horizontal street at the left, with two right-turn arrows), with NO.1 LANE WIDTH, CURB LANE (OR NO.2 & NO.3 COMBINED) WIDTH, a 1' dimension and the same 20' and 12' minimums. In the intersection, dashed cat track lines run diagonally, with SEE NOTE 6 and ALTERNATIVE LOCATIONS FOR CAT TRACKS callouts, and SEE NOTE 9 pointing at the diagonal cat track. Two left-turn arrows are shown on the right edge of the detail.

description:
The sheet is drawn rotated 90 degrees, with the three plan views stacked left to right and the approach to the railroad crossing running toward the top of the rotated drawing (the text reads sideways).

Two-lane road plan (left view): A roadway with a dashed centerline and a lane on each side, a parking lane on the right shown with a parked car symbol, and an Edge of traveled lane, Parking lane or shoulder label. A pair of railroad tracks crosses the road at an angle at the bottom of the plan. Railroad limit lines (heavy transverse bars) are placed 15' from edge of rail or 8' from gate, shown on both approaches with the callout. Advance markings in the traveled lane consist of the paired RXR symbols (an X with R on each side, two symbols per lane) between bar lines. Two bar lines are labeled Bar Line, each placed 90 degrees to the lane (callouts 90 degrees), with 2' dimensions shown between bar lines and from the limit line. A W10-1 and W48(CA) (if applicable) sign callout sits at the start of the markings. A dimension of 50' is shown, with See Table A, for the distance back from the limit line to the sign. The bottom approach shows the same arrangement in the other direction.

Multilane road with angled crossing (center view): Two traffic lanes with dashed lane lines on each side of the centerline and a curb on each side (labeled Curb). The tracks cross at an angle. Railroad limit lines are drawn angled parallel to the tracks. The callout 15' from edge of rail or 8' from gate. For angled crossings of 60 degrees or greater, install as shown to left. The angled limit lines meet the lane edge, with the lane line at the curb. A Bar Line is 90 degrees to the lane and the RXR symbols (three per lane) are placed in the lane between bar lines. A dimension See Table A is shown from the limit line. At the right edge, a callout says Striped full time or peak hour curb lane. A W10-1 and W48(CA) (if applicable) callout is repeated.

Multilane approach (right view): A multilane approach with three paired RXR symbols (R X R X R X in a row, i.e. three RXR symbols) per lane between a Bar Line and a second bar line, with See Table A distance and a Striped full time or peak hour curb lane callout, W10-1 and W48(CA) (if applicable) at the start of the markings.

Sign details: W10-1 is the circular railroad crossing advance warning sign with a black X and R R. W48(CA) is a rectangular sign TRACKS with a 2 in a tab above (2 TRACKS), labeled Install if two or more tracks.

Table A (posted speed in mph and distance in feet): 25 mph: 50 ft. 30 mph: 50 ft. 35 mph: 125 ft. 40 mph: 175 ft. 45 mph: 250 ft. 50 mph: 325 ft. 55 mph: 400 ft. The heading is marked with an asterisk.

notes:
1. Signs shall have Diamond Grade or Type VIII retro-reflective white lettering and numbers on a standard blue Type IV retro-reflective background with match component UV/anti-graffiti film. For Type A signs, all colors shall be provided in the official 4" diameter City Seal. Signs shall be provided with a 10-year replacement warranty against wear, delamination or fading. An LADOT-approved vendor shall be used for fabrication.
2. The sign blade material shall be 1/8 inch thick aluminum stock.
3. Letters and numbers shall be Highway Series B, with at least one stroke width between letters (45% spacing). For Type A signs, the initial upper case letters shall be 6" and the lower case letters shall be 4.5", except as discussed in Note 9. For Type B signs, the initial upper case letters shall be 4" and the lower case letters shall be 3". Intermediate (non-first) words such as "of", "the", "el", "la", "los", "las", "de" and "del" shall have all lower case letters. The block number and upper case letter representing the cardinal address direction, if any, shall be 3". The space between words shall be same width as an upper case letter "O". The legend shall appear on both sides of the aluminum blade. The street name text shall be left justified starting a minimum of 2" from left edge of sign. The legend may be centered.
4. Numbered streets shall be indicated by Arabic numerals and not letters. Where the number appears before the title (such as 3 rd Street or 4 th Avenue) the number shall be followed by an ordinal abbreviation, "st", "nd", "rd" or "th", at the same level, with a space between them. However, where the number appears after the title (such as Avenue 19), an ordinal abbreviation shall not be used. The space shall be the same width as an uppercase letter "O".
5. The block number shall be followed by an upper case letter representing the cardinal direction, only where the named street has address numbers in another direction (such as for Sepulveda Boulevard, Vermont Avenue, Olympic Boulevard, 3rd Street, etc.) within the City of Los Angeles or an adjacent city. The space between the block number and the upper case letter representing the cardinal direction shall be the same width as upper case "O".
6. Where the named street is a private street or driveway, the block number shall be replaced by "PVT" in 3" upper case letters.
7. Apostrophes shall be used, where appropriate. Accent and tilde markings shall be provided for non-English words and names, where appropriate. A lower case "i" or "j" shall be dotted.
8. The Bureau of Engineering is the source for street names. If a private street or driveway requires a name, due to signalization or some other reason, the Bureau of Engineering must process the naming proposal.
9. The following street name abbreviations shall be used, except where using the unabbreviated word would not require an increase in sign length (such as "B Street"). Periods shall not be used after abbreviations.
Word : abbreviation
Alley: (No abbreviation)
Avenida: (No abbreviation)

Avenue (first word): (No abbreviation)
Boulevard: Bl

Canyon (first word): (No abbreviation)

Court (other than end word): (No abbreviation)
Drive: Dr

General (when used as a title): Gen
Heights: Hgts

Junior (as part of a name): Jr
Lane: (No abbreviation)

Paseo: (No abbreviation)

Plaza: (No abbreviation)

Street: St

title: Street Name Signs, Notes 1 to 9 and Abbreviation Table
summary: Sheet 4 of 9 of the street name sign standard gives Notes 1 to 9: retro-reflective sheeting, 1/8 inch aluminum blade, Highway Series B lettering and sizes, numbered street and block number rules, PVT for private streets, and the Bureau of Engineering as the source of names. It ends with the required abbreviation table, such as Av, Bl, Dr, St and Pl.

description:
Notes page, no drawing. It continues Note 9 with the cardinal direction rule, then gives Note 10 with a table of blade length by text length, and Notes 11, 12 and 13.
Table (Note 10): The blade length should be determined using the table below. Columns: text including interword spaces (characters), blade length for Type A one-line signs, blade length for Type B signs. Rows: 9 or less: 30" and 30". 10: 36" and 30". 11, 12: 42" and 30". 13, 14: 48" and 36". 15, 16: 54" and 36". 17, 18: 60" and 42". 19, 20: * and 48". 21, 22: * and 54". 23, 24: * and 54". 25, 26: * and 60".
notes:
9. (continued) In addition, cardinal direction names may be abbreviated to "N", "S", "E" or "W", only where the unabbreviated word would require the sign length to exceed 60". For example, use "Huntington Dr S" (abbreviated) and "Cahuenga Bl East" (unabbreviated).
10. The blade length should be determined using the table below. (Table as listed in the description.)
* Longer street names for Type A signs shall use two-line blades. The width of the two-line blade shall be based on the text of the longer line. The maximum length of a two-line blade shall be 48 inches. Where the text of the longer line of a two-line blade exceeds 14 characters, 4" upper case and 3" lower case letters may be used.
11. Type A and Type B signs that are 30" or 36" long shall be side-mounted only, as shown on sheets 6 and 7. Type A and Type B signs that are 42" and longer shall be side-mounted with vertical support, as shown on sheets 8 and 9. Minor deviations in the sign brackets shown are permissible only with the prior written approval of LADOT.
12. When provided for initial installation, replacement or maintenance, Type A signs shall be used at intersections when at least one approach is a designated Major, Secondary or Collector Street. When provided for initial installation, replacement or maintenance, Type B signs shall be used at intersections where all approaches are designated Local Streets.
13. Street name signs shall be provided on the near-right side of each leg of a primary street at the named crossing street, flagged in the direction of the sidewalk or parkway, unless it is physically infeasible. If so, an alternate location shall be provided. If the named cross street does not intersect the primary street, due to a separation island, an additional near-right sign shall be provided on the island. For unusual situations, see S-221.3.
title: Street Name Signs, Notes 9 (continued) to 13 and Blade Length Table
summary: Sheet 5 of 9 of the street name sign standard finishes Note 9 on abbreviating cardinal directions and gives the Note 10 table of blade length by number of characters for Type A and Type B signs, from 30 to 60 inches.
